root_cause_label: Two-Level Distribution Model Cannot Satisfy Dual KL Constraints
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent immediately adopted a two-level parametric distribution (k elements at probability alpha, rest uniform) that lacks the degrees of freedom to simultaneously satisfy both KL(P||U)=10.0 and KL(U||P)=10.0, and despite 30+ steps of optimization thrashing never recognized that a three-level model is required.
t_err_evidence: Writes find_distribution.py adopting flawed k-element parametrization and buggy backward-KL formula using np.mean(np.log(p_safe)).
t_commit_evidence: From step 2 onward the agent never escapes the fundamental two-level model paradigm. All subsequent scripts (v2 through v9, fine_tune, exponential decay) are variations of the same insufficient model class. The failing outcome is locked in from this first implementation choice.
t_surface_evidence: WARNING: Distribution does not meet tolerance requirements; Forward KL error: 1.224230
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed without verification that a two-level distribution (k elements with uniform high probability, remaining V-k elements sharing the leftover mass equally) would be expressive enough to satisfy two independent KL divergence constraints. This is false: with only 2 free parameters, you cannot independently control both KL(P||U) (which depends on the entropy of P) and KL(U||P) (which depends on the average log of P). A three-level model is needed, but the agent never reasoned through this analytically.
